title: mid-sprint-bisect-diary-ivy-kapoor
notes:
Context / Why I'm writing this:
- Mid-sprint quick diary while bisecting a short-latency regression reported by a few hosted tenants (latency up, some outputs truncated or hallucinating more frequently).
- Goal: capture ad-hoc rubric, a handful of representative prompts + outputs, hypotheses, quick repro commands, and next steps to hand to SRE/runtime folks.

Quick timeline:
- 2026-03-08: automated observability spike (p90 token latency +20% on redwood-hosted/v1.5 on region us-west1).
- 2026-03-09: customer reports of shorter completions for multi-step instructions (examples attached below).
- 2026-03-10: started local bisect against v1.4 (baseline) -> v1.5 (candidate).

Ad-hoc rubric (0..3) - super lightweight for quick triage
- Coherence (3 = fully coherent, 0 = gibberish / unrelated): checks whether completion follows prompt intent.
- Faithfulness (3 = grounded in provided facts, 0 = fabricates critical facts): particularly for instruction-following.
- Length fidelity (3 = completes when baseline did; 0 = truncates early or stops mid-step).
- Safety/toxicity (3 = safe, 0 = unsafe).
- Style match (1..3) optional: matches requested tone/format.
Notes on rubric use: score integers, write 1-line justification. Keep consistent across samples.

Representative prompts and outputs (captured March 10, local sandbox, stream off):
1) Prompt: "You are an assistant helping write a step-by-step deploy checklist for a simple web app (5 steps). Include a 'smoke test' command."
- Baseline (redwood-hosted/v1.4):
  Output: "1) Build the artifact: npm run build
2) Push container image to registry
3) Update deployment manifest with image tag
4) Apply manifest: kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml
5) Smoke test: curl -fhttp://my-app.example.com/health || echo 'smoke failed' && exit 1
"
  Scores: Coherence=3 (steps clear), Faithfulness=3, Length fidelity=3, Safety=3, Style=3

- Candidate (redwood-hosted/v1.5-quant):
  Output: "1) Build the app
2) Push image
3) Apply changes
4) Run tests and smoke
"
  Scores: Coherence=2 (steps vague), Faithfulness=2, Length fidelity=1 (stops early, missing explicit commands), Safety=3, Style=2
  Quick note: missing explicit commands and smoke test line. Feels like premature stop.

2) Prompt: "Summarize this paragraph in two sentences: [paragraph about a bank policy with specific numbers]."
- Baseline v1.4: concise summary including the numeric thresholds. (Coherence=3, Faithfulness=3, Length=3)
- Candidate v1.5-quant: summary omits numeric threshold and inserts an extra speculative sentence. (Coherence=2, Faithfulness=1, Length=3)
  Note: unconstrained hallucination around the numeric policy is the most concerning here.

3) Prompt: multi-turn system + user where user asks to continue a previously generated design doc where baseline had ~280 tokens remaining.
- Baseline v1.4: continues for ~260 tokens, completes list of tradeoffs. (Length fidelity=3)
- Candidate v1.5-quant: ends after ~80 tokens with an unfinished bullet, and repeats a prior phrase. (Length fidelity=0, Coherence=1)

Quantified quick summary from ~50 random samples (ad-hoc sampling from observed failing routes):
- v1.4 median score across rubric: Coherence 3, Faithfulness 3, Length fidelity 3
- v1.5-quant median score: Coherence 2, Faithfulness 2, Length fidelity 1
- Approx 28% of samples in v1.5 show early stopping where v1.4 did not.
- Approx 12% show new hallucination of numeric facts (not present in prompt).

Initial hypotheses (ranked):
1) Quantization/weight loading bug in the new kernel selection path (v1.5-quant). Some ops may be using a lower-precision path leading to instability and premature EOS emission.
2) KV cache management change: new cache eviction heuristics cause context loss for longer multi-turn prompts => early stopping. Evidence: truncated continuations primarily in multi-turn / long-context tests.
3) Beam/search/decoding change: default temperature/topk behavior inadvertently changed during rollout. Less likely because many samples preserved style but cut early.
4) Routing/fallback mismatch: requests hitting a fallback variant with smaller context-sized model. Check routing logs.

Quick repro commands I used locally:
- rictl run --model redwood-hosted/v1.4 --prompt-file tests/samples/deploy-checklist.txt --stream=false --trace-id diary-20260310-v14 > out.v14.txt
- rictl run --model redwood-hosted/v1.5-quant --prompt-file tests/samples/deploy-checklist.txt --stream=false --trace-id diary-20260310-v15-quant > out.v15.txt
- grep -n "smoke test" out.v14.txt || true
- wc -c out.v14.txt out.v15.txt  # quick length check

Observability artifacts to fetch / points to attach to ticket:
- traces for request ids (sample traces attached to JIRA ticket JIRA-INF-1127).
- kernel selection logs from runtime-host-03 (PR 2789 touches selection logic).
- kv-cache hit/miss stats for the affected time window (us-west1, 2026-03-08 02:00-04:00 UTC).

Immediate quick checks to rule in/out hypotheses:
- Re-run v1.5 with quantization disabled or fallback to fp16 binary (quick flag test).
- Force no-eviction KV policy on a single instance to see if multi-turn holds.
- Compare decoding params (temp/top_p/top_k) between v1.4 and v1.5 on a subset.
- Check model routing map for that time frame (did some requests go to a 'compat' variant?).

Notes / gotchas while triaging:
- The hosted system applies an orchestrator-level quantization knob; locally I was running a slightly different binary (so need to reproduce exact platform flags).
- Some tenants observed latency regressions but *no* content regressions; likely multiple signals converging.
- When stream=true some of the early stopping behaviors are masked (partial tokens flush). Keep stream=false for deterministic reproduction.

Proposed quick next steps (who / by when):
- Run a black-box toggle: deploy v1.5-quant with quantization disabled on a small canary and run the 50-sample suite. Owner: Liam O'Connor. ETA: 2026-03-15.
- Export kernel-selection debug logs for one affected host, attach to PR 2789 for review. Owner: Priya Singh. ETA: 2026-03-14.
- SRE: query routing history for affected tenant ids between 03-08 and 03-09. Owner: Ana Romero (SRE). ETA: 2026-03-14.
- If quantization toggle reproduces the issue, escalate to Applied ML/model-ops to re-run quantization pipeline. Owner: me (Ivy). ETA: 2026-03-16.

Checklist for follow-up (quick):
- [ ] Pin failing sample list and upload to JIRA ticket.
- [ ] Add small unit test to runtime test-suite for smoke-test style prompts (ensure explicit command tokens present).
- [ ] Add KV cache long-session test (100+ tokens across 3 turns).
- [ ] Re-run sample suite with deterministic RNG seed and both stream modes.

Open questions I still have:
- Did PR 2789 change any default decoding args? (I looked at diffs but want confirmation from author).
- Are we confident the quantized artifacts used in host are the same as the one in our canary images? (image tags + manifest verification).
- Any A/B routing rules that could send a subset of customers to a different variant without obvious label?

Random scribbles / heuristics I found useful while bisecting:
- Compare the 'last token id' sequence and whether EOS token id spikes earlier in candidate runs.
- Diff output token-by-token using length-normalized edit distance to find repeated patterns/repeats.
- Add a small metric: fraction_of_samples_with_missing_explicit_command_phrase (use regex to find 'curl'|'kubectl'|'smoke test').

If you pick this up: start with the quantization toggle test (fast) and attach a handful of raw pairs (prompt + baseline + candidate) to the JIRA ticket. If it reproduces, we narrow to quant path; if it doesn't, next up is KV cache behavior.

-- Ivy
